adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests pass only because they invoke the controller directly with a fabricated group_id param that the route never produces, hiding the param mismatch

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds member routes under `resources :groups`:
- `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`
- `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`
In Rails this generates URLs like `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`, so the router *does* supply `params[:group_id]`, matching `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` and `#remove_member` which call `params.require(:group_id)`. The JS also hits `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json`, which maps to the same `:group_id` segment. Therefore the tests using `group_id:` are consistent with the route; there’s no hidden param mismatch shown by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new usage of `{{fa-icon ...}}` in `admin/templates/group.hbs` and `admin/templates/group_member.hbs`, but it does not show whether the `fa-icon` helper exists or not elsewhere in the codebase. Since the finding hinges on repository-wide absence of the helper (not demonstrated in this diff), the claimed render error is not verifiable from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create action silently discards the alias_level param sent by the frontend, so groups are always created with alias_level 0 regardless of selection

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#create`, the new group only sets `name` and `visible` (and saves), but never applies `params[:alias_level]`. Meanwhile the frontend `Discourse.Group#create()` POSTs `data: this.asJSON()`, and `asJSON()` includes `alias_level`. As a result, any alias level selected in the UI is ignored on creation and the group will keep the model/default alias_level (effectively 0).

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller members endpoint response contract rewritten (new meta envelope, limit 200→50, automatic-group special-casing removed) with no spec coverage for it

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a concrete contract change in `GroupsController#members`: it now returns an envelope `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` instead of `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (and it changes the default limit from 200/automatic-only paging to always paginated with default 50). This is relied on by new client code (`Discourse.Group#findMembers` now requests `/groups/:name/members.json` and reads `result.meta` / `result.members`). However, the diff adds/updates specs only for `Admin::GroupsController` and does not add any spec coverage for `GroupsController#members` response shape/semantics, so regressions in this endpoint’s contract wouldn’t be caught.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ADVISORY: group_member.hbs {{#unless automatic}} relies on Ember controller-scope fallback since the item is a Discourse.User with no automatic property, making the remove link UI guard fragile and untested

adjudication.rationale: In the new `group_member.hbs`, the guard `{{#unless automatic}}` is unqualified, while the item being rendered is a `member` (a `Discourse.User`) and the `group-member` view (`admin/views/group-member.js.es6`) does not define/bind an `automatic` property. That means the template is implicitly depending on Ember’s context/controller fallback to resolve `automatic` from the parent group controller/model. This is a diff-grounded scope coupling that could easily break if the view/controller context changes, and it’s not explicitly wired (e.g., `automatic=automatic` or `controller.automatic`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Creating a group with initial members capability was silently removed: create() no longer sends usernames and controller no longer reads params[:group][:usernames], so admin-entered usernames are silently discarded; the corresponding test was deleted rather than replaced

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the prior “create group + usernames” flow (JS `createWithUsernames`/`saveWithUsernames` removed; `Admin::GroupsController#create` no longer reads `params[:group][:usernames]`), but it is not “silently discarding admin-entered usernames”: the new admin template only shows the member add UI when `{{#if id}}` (i.e., after the group exists), and member changes are now handled explicitly via new endpoints (`add_members`/`remove_member`) with new specs. The old create-with-members test was replaced by create-name-stripping and new add/remove member tests, not simply deleted without replacement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated formatting-only reindentation of templates and SCSS restructuring misleads bisect/blame, and the SCSS move broadened .badges-scoped rules into a shared .groups, .badges selector, creating hidden coupling between badge pages and admin group pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include large template reindentation/whitespace-only changes (e.g. `user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs`, `admin-group-selector.hbs`) which can add noise for blame/bisect. More concretely, the SCSS change moves generic `.form-horizontal` styling into a combined selector `.groups, .badges { .form-horizontal { ... } }` (in `admin_base.scss`), which explicitly shares styling between the groups and badges sections and therefore creates cross-page coupling in CSS scope. This is a maintainability/scope concern rather than a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination math Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 renders an empty phantom page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit, incorrectly disabling/enabling the next-page control

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` (when `user_count != 0`). If `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100/50), this yields an extra page (3 instead of 2). This interacts with `showingLast` (`propertyEqual("currentPage","totalPages")`) and `actions.next`, which advances `offset` up to `user_count` (`min(offset+limit, user_count)`). That allows `offset == user_count`, and `Group.findMembers` then requests that offset, producing an empty members list (phantom page) and incorrect next/previous enablement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group members route sets controller model to a Group instead of the members array without a GroupMembersController defining a members property, risking an empty public members table if proxying doesn't resolve; no spec covers groups_controller#members

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members, GroupUserSerializer)` to a new JSON envelope with `members:` and `meta:` (limit/offset/total), but no corresponding spec is added/updated to cover this new response contract. The claim that the public members table will be empty due to the route setting `controller.model` to a `Group` is plausible (route now does `controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers();` while the template iterates `members`), but whether `members` resolves depends on the (not-shown) controller type/proxying, so the empty-table bug is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages computation uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 instead of Math.ceil(user_count / limit), causing a phantom empty last page when member count is an exact multiple of the limit

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100 users, limit 50), this returns 3 instead of 2, creating a phantom extra page. This matches the finding; the correct computation should use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the existing `user_count == 0` guard).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking unversioned API contract change: /groups/:group_id/members response shape changes from a bare JSON array to an object with members and meta keys, with no version bump or content negotiation

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes GroupsController#members from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which would return a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, altering the response shape for `/groups/:group_id/members` without any visible versioning/content-negotiation mechanism in this diff. Internal JS callers were updated to expect `result.meta` and `result.members`, but any other existing consumers of the unversioned endpoint would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleted get "users" route alias in config/routes.rb with no deprecation path

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `get "users"` route under the admin groups resource in `config/routes.rb` and replaces it with `delete "members"` / `put "members"` (i.e., the old endpoint is no longer routed). The diff does not show any compatibility alias, redirect, or deprecation handling for the removed `GET` route, so this is a potentially breaking change for any existing callers, though not necessarily an internal correctness bug based solely on the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips unknown usernames and returns success_json, giving admins no feedback about failed username resolution

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are iterated via `usernames.split(",")` and only added if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; unknown usernames are simply ignored (`if user = ...`). The action then returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if some/all usernames didn’t resolve, so the client gets no per-username failure feedback. This is a UX/behavioral gap rather than a clear correctness defect (and prior specs even asserted silent success for non-existent users in the removed incremental update tests).

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 query loop in add_members: one User.find_by_username per username plus individual group.add(user) inserts, instead of a bulk query and bulk insert

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the diff adds `usernames.split(",").each` and for each username performs `User.find_by_username(username)` and then `group.add(user)` (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb). This is an N-per-username lookup pattern (and likely per-user membership insert) rather than a bulk `WHERE username IN (...)` + bulk association insert. It’s a performance/scalability concern, but not a functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member spec uses xhr :put but the route is registered as DELETE, testing a verb combination no production caller uses and asserting a status the route cannot produce via that verb

adjudication.rationale: In routes.rb the admin group member removal endpoint is registered as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, while the controller spec under `context ".remove_member"` calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`. That test exercises `remove_member` with a PUT verb that no production route maps to, so it’s not validating the real request/route combination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group_member.hbs relies on Handlebars context-chain fallthrough for 'automatic' property since the member context (Discourse.User) has no automatic attribute, making the remove link's visibility fragile and accidental

adjudication.rationale: In `group_member.hbs`, the remove link is wrapped in `{{#unless automatic}} ... {{/unless}}` while the per-item context is a `member` (a `Discourse.User` created in `group.findMembers()`), which does not have an `automatic` attribute in this diff. Since `group.hbs` renders members via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, `automatic` must be resolved via Handlebars/Ember context-chain lookup from the surrounding controller/model. That will likely work today but is implicitly coupled to template scoping rules and is not explicit/robust (e.g., passing `automatic` into the item view).

adjudication_records.issue_text: setupController no longer returns model.findMembers() and afterModel hook was deleted, so the route resolves before members load and the template renders against undefined
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both describe that findMembers() is now async/unhandled so the route/controller proceeds before members are loaded, leading to a race condition where the template/controller may see undefined member data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers() now returns undefined instead of a resolved promise (previously Ember.RSVP.resolve([])) when name is empty, so any caller chaining .then on it throws

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers` changed from `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([]);` to a bare `return;` when `name` is empty, so it can now return `undefined` instead of a thenable. While the diff also removes the in-diff callers that were chaining `.then(...)` (the `afterModel` hooks were deleted), this is still a contract change that could break any other existing callers expecting a promise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public /groups/:group_id/members endpoint now caps all groups at 50 members with no pagination controls in the user-facing template, silently truncating lists for groups larger than 50

adjudication.rationale: In GroupsController#members, the endpoint now always applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, for all groups (not just automatic), so a request with no params returns only 50 members. On the client side, `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` calls `model.findMembers()` but does not set `limit/offset`, and the user-facing template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` simply iterates `{{#each m in members}}` with no pagination UI/controls added here. This will silently truncate member lists for groups > 50.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed PATCH verb and changes:{add/delete} handling from admin groups update deletes a previously accepted API contract with no deprecation or versioning, breaking existing API clients

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes PATCH-specific handling for incremental membership updates. In `Admin::GroupsController`, the prior `update` method branched on `request.patch?` and processed `params[:changes][:add]`/`[:delete]` (see removed `update_patch` and the old `update` dispatcher). After the change, `update` only accepts top-level `alias_level`, `visible`, and (non-automatic) `name`, and there is no `changes` handling. Since Rails routes for a resource `update` typically accept PATCH by default, existing API clients using PATCH with `changes:{add/delete}` would now silently stop working (membership won’t change), i.e., a backwards-incompatible behavioral break introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Automatic-group membership changes now return 422 instead of the prior 403, and the spec pinning the 403 behavior was deleted without an equivalent 422 test being re-established

adjudication.rationale: While the diff does change the response for automatic-group membership modifications to 422 via `can_not_modify_automatic` in `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` and `#remove_member`, the claim that the 403-pinning spec was removed “without an equivalent 422 test” is contradicted by the added specs: `context ".add_members"` includes `response.status.should == 422`, and `context ".remove_member"` also asserts `response.status.should == 422` for automatic groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Specs pinning silent-success behavior for adding non-existent users / removing non-members were dropped rather than rewritten, losing the intent record even though behavior survived

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the prior incremental update spec cases that explicitly asserted silent-success behavior (e.g., adding a non-existent user and removing a non-member) under the old PATCH-based API. In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, the entire `context 'incremental'` block (including “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users” and “succeeds silently when removing non-members”) is deleted and not replaced with equivalent tests for the new endpoints (`add_members`, `remove_member`). The new implementation still appears to be silent for missing users (`add_members` only adds when `User.find_by_username` returns a user) and likely no-ops for non-members (`group.users.delete(user_id)`), but that intent is no longer captured by specs, reducing coverage/contract clarity for the changed API.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member spec issues a PUT (xhr :put) but the route only maps DELETE for remove_member (PUT is bound to add_members), so the test exercises the wrong route and certifies intent the API does not implement

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` under `context ".remove_member"`, the first example calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`. But `config/routes.rb` maps `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` under the admin groups resource. So the spec uses the wrong HTTP verb for the implemented route; it can pass while the real DELETE endpoint behavior remains untested (and a PUT request to that path would not route to `remove_member`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers empty-name early return changed from a resolved promise to a bare return (undefined), breaking callers that relied on a promise and rendering an empty/broken member list

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `Discourse.Group#findMembers` from returning `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` when `name` is empty to a bare `return` (undefined): `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`. This is a behavioral/contract change: callers that previously could always treat `findMembers()` as thenable (as was done before via `afterModel(...).then(...)`) can now break on empty-name cases. Even in this diff, actions like `next/previous` in `admin-group.js.es6` do `return group.findMembers();` which will now return undefined in that edge case, potentially breaking any upstream chaining/UI state handling that expects a promise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group-members route setupController changed the controller model from resolved members to the group with a fire-and-forget findMembers(), so the user-facing page renders an empty table until the async call lands with no loading state

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`, the route no longer waits for `model.findMembers()` in `afterModel`; it now sets `controller.set("model", model)` and calls `model.findMembers()` without chaining/awaiting. The template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` was changed to iterate `{{#each m in members}}`, which will be empty/undefined on initial render until `findMembers()` populates `model.members`. There is no loading conditional/state added in the diff, so a brief empty table flash is a plausible UX regression, but it won’t necessarily throw or permanently break rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: params.require(:usernames).split(",") in add_members crashes with NoMethodError when usernames is an Array (e.g. usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b), causing a 500 on malformed input

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff adds `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",").each` (see `add_members`). If a client submits `usernames` as an Array (e.g. `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), `params.require(:usernames)` will be an Array and `split` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500. This behavior is directly implied by the new code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-existent usernames are silently ignored in add_members, returning success_json with no feedback about which usernames failed, leaving API consumers with an incomplete membership change

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record; missing usernames are simply skipped with no error tracking. The action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, providing no feedback about which provided usernames were invalid. This is verifiable in the diff, but it’s more of an API/UX contract concern than a definite functional defect (the earlier spec suite even had a test asserting silent success for non-existent users, which was removed here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member spec uses xhr :put but route is DELETE; Rails controller specs bypass routing so the actual DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members route wiring is untested

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, the first `.remove_member` example calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but the routes added in `config/routes.rb` wire member removal as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (i.e., DELETE). Because controller specs invoke the action directly, this mismatch won’t catch incorrect HTTP verb/route wiring; the spec is therefore not accurately exercising the new DELETE route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members nil branch (non-existent username) is untested; prior spec covering silent-skip was deleted with no replacement

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, usernames are split and each is conditionally added only if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user, silently skipping non-existent usernames (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`). The prior spec explicitly asserting this behavior (“succeeds silently when adding non-existent users”) was removed with the deletion of the incremental PATCH tests, and the new `.add_members` specs only cover adding valid users and automatic-group rejection—no replacement test covers the skip-on-missing-user branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create specs deleted rather than ported; render_json_error failure branch and params[:visible] handling for invalid creates have no coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, the prior `.create` coverage that asserted full group creation behavior (previously including usernames) was removed and replaced with only a single test asserting whitespace stripping (`context ".create"` only tests `name: " bob "`). In `Admin::GroupsController#create`, there is an explicit failure branch (`else render_json_error group`) and parsing of `visible` (`group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`), but the updated specs do not exercise an invalid create (e.g., missing/invalid name) nor any `visible` parameter combinations. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips unknown/typo'd usernames, returning success without reporting skipped names, causing silent membership data loss

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are split and each is added only if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; unknown/typo’d usernames are silently ignored (`if user = ...; group.add(user); end`). The action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, with no indication of which usernames were skipped. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral issue, but it doesn’t demonstrate actual “membership data loss” in the diff—just lack of feedback/validation for invalid usernames.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) on a has_many :through, bypassing model callbacks/validations on the join record

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` removing a user via `group.users.delete(user_id)`. In Rails, `association.delete` typically deletes the join row directly and does not run callbacks/validations that would run with `destroy`/`destroy_all` on the join model. The diff does not show the `Group`↔`User` association or any join-model callbacks, so the impact (whether anything important is skipped) can’t be verified here, but the concern is diff-grounded and specific.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member silently succeeds when the user is not a member, giving stale UI a false success response

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds, regardless of whether the user was actually in the group. That “silent success” is consistent with an idempotent DELETE and isn’t clearly a defect based on the diff alone. Also, the UI code (`Discourse.Group#removeMember`) reloads the member list via `self.findMembers()` on success, so the claim about “stale UI” being left in a false-success state is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: API contract change shipped as a cutover: new update endpoint drops usernames handling while old PUT format is silently swallowed (200 success) instead of rejected, risking silent data loss for existing clients and during rolling deploys

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes usernames handling from the existing PUT /admin/groups/:id update path but still returns success. Previously, `update_put` read `payload = params[:group]` and applied `group.usernames = payload[:usernames]` (and name/visible/alias_level). Now `update` reads only top-level `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]` and never inspects `params[:group]` or `:usernames` (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb). As a result, an older client sending the old PUT payload (`group: { usernames: ... }`) would have membership changes silently ignored while `group.save` can still succeed and return 200, which matches the finding’s “silently swallowed” / “risking silent data loss” concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently drops unknown usernames: failed find_by_username lookups are skipped without any error, log, or partial-failure list while the endpoint still returns success_json

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are split and each is looked up via `User.find_by_username(username)`; if the user is not found, the code simply does nothing (`if user = ...; group.add(user); end`) and proceeds to `group.save` and returns `success_json` on save. There is no error/partial-failure reporting for unknown usernames, so the finding is accurate, but this behavior also existed in the previous incremental update logic (now removed), making it more of an API/UX concern than a newly introduced correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members has no bound on the usernames payload, allowing a huge comma-separated list to trigger thousands of sequential queries and inserts in one request

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the new endpoint accepts `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then does `usernames.split(",").each` with a `User.find_by_username(username)` lookup and `group.add(user)` per entry, with no limit on count/length. This allows a very large comma-separated payload to drive an unbounded number of DB lookups and membership additions in a single request (potential DoS/performance/security issue) introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group members pagination (findMembers, next/previous) has no in-flight guard, so overlapping requests race and last-response-wins can display the wrong page with no error

adjudication.rationale: The new pagination actions in `admin-group.js.es6` (`next`/`previous`) mutate `group.offset` and immediately call `group.findMembers()`, which performs an async `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` and unconditionally `setProperties({ members, offset, ... })` on resolution. There is no in-flight guard (e.g., tracking the latest request/promise, disabling navigation while loading, or cancelling prior requests), so multiple rapid clicks can issue overlapping requests whose responses may resolve out of order and overwrite `members/offset` with stale data (last-response-wins), displaying the wrong page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client addMembers discards the returned promise with no failure feedback or rollback, and never clears the usernames input on success, so failures are invisible and retries re-submit the same list

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` but does not `return` the promise or attach any `.then/.catch` handling, so AJAX failures would have no UI feedback. The diff also explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and never resets `usernames` on success, so retries would re-submit the same list. This is a concrete, diff-grounded UX/robustness issue rather than a clearly broken behavior shown by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member returns success_json even for a nonexistent or non-member user_id, making 'already removed' indistinguishable from a successful removal

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code unconditionally does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds (which it typically will even if nothing was deleted). There is no check that the user exists or is a member of the group, so the endpoint is effectively idempotent and cannot distinguish “removed” vs “already not a member / nonexistent user_id”. Whether that’s a defect depends on intended API semantics; the diff shows the behavior but not that it’s incorrect.
